icse_10_scheme.subjects_and_marks: Group I compulsory: English, a Second Language, History Civics & Geography - each 80% external / 20% internal. Group II (any two/three per regulations): Mathematics, Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology), Economics, Commercial Studies, Modern Foreign Language, Classical Language, Environmental Science - 80/20. Group III (one subject from Section A or B, or two): 50% external / 50% internal. Internal assessment by school from assignments, projects, practicals, coursework (e.g. 100-mark subject = 80-mark paper + 20 internal, 10 teacher + 10 external examiner). Exact number of Group II subjects required: unverified.

isc_12_scheme.subjects_and_marks: English (801) or Modern English (891) compulsory: Paper I theory 3 h 80 marks + Project 20 marks. Plus four or five elective subjects; max six subjects including English. Elective theory/practical splits (commonly 70/30 for sciences) unverified - check each subject PDF.

ssc_10_pattern.known: MSBSHSE Pune enters practical, oral, grading and internal evaluation marks separately from the written SSC exam; the Board Act (1965) lets its committee fix max/min marks, time and duration for written, oral and practical tests. An 80 written + 20 internal split per subject could NOT be confirmed on an official page.

dpdp_children.act_section: DPDP Act 2023 s.9: (1) before processing any personal data of a child (under 18, s.2(f)) obtain verifiable consent of the parent/lawful guardian in the prescribed manner; (2) no processing likely to cause detrimental effect on a child's well-being; (3) no tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children; (4) govt may exempt classes of fiduciaries/purposes from (1) and (3); (5) govt may notify a lower age for a fiduciary whose processing is 'verifiably safe'. Penalty for child obligations up to Rs 200 crore (PIB).

rules.notification: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 - G.S.R. 846(E), dated New Delhi 13 November 2025 (PIB says notified 14 November 2025, i.e. Gazette publication)
rules.commencement: Rules 1, 2, 17-21 on publication; Rule 4 (Consent Managers) one year after publication; Rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23 eighteen months after publication (rule 1(2)-(4)) => child-consent Rule 10 and exemptions Rule 12 in force ~13/14 May 2027
rules.verifiable_parental_consent_rule: Rule 10: fiduciary must adopt technical and organisational measures so verifiable consent of the parent is obtained BEFORE processing a child's data, and do due diligence that the person claiming to be the parent is an identifiable adult (18+), by reference to (a) reliable identity/age details already held by the fiduciary, or (b) identity/age details voluntarily given by the individual or via a virtual token mapped to such details issued by an authorised entity (incl. one verified by a Digital Locker service provider, e.g. DigiLocker). Rule 11 covers lawful guardians of persons with disability.
rules.education_exemptions: Rule 12 + Fourth Schedule. Part A (class exemptions from s.9(1) and 9(3)): item 3 'educational institution' - processing restricted to tracking and behavioural monitoring (a) for the educational activities of such institution or (b) in the interests of safety of enrolled children; item 4 creche/day-care; item 5 transport provider engaged by an educational institution - location tracking during travel. 'Educational institution' = an institution of learning that imparts education, incl. vocational. Part B (purpose exemptions) includes: functions under law in a child's interest, subsidies/benefits/certificates under s.7(b), creating an email-only user account, real-time location for safety, blocking harmful content/ads, and confirming a user is NOT a child. NOTE: the exemption is narrow - it does not cover a general ed-tech app (not itself an educational institution) collecting children's data; such an app needs Rule 10 parental consent. PIB's summary ('unless ... essential services such as healthcare, education') is broader than the rule text.
